xmldoc.short_description: Write a recording in the EDF+ format.

param_input_item.param_description: the path of the EDF+ file to write.
a recording struct, as ecglab.readedf returns.
the length of a data record in seconds (one by default).

param_output_item.param_description: what was laid down: the number of records, the samples per record, the physical range used for each lead and the quantisation it implies, and whether the last record was padded.

description.p: EDF is what a recorder and a sleep or Holter laboratory writes, so a recording built or processed in the module is written to EDF+C to be opened by any EDF tool and read back by ecglab.readedf without loss beyond the quantisation.

The physical range of each lead is its own minimum and maximum with a small margin, so the extreme values are not pinned to the digital rails, and the digital range is the full signed sixteen bit -32768..32767. The quantisation is therefore (pmax - pmin) / 65535, which info reports per lead, so a caller knows the reconstruction error without re-reading the file.
The patient field is recording.info.subject, written X X X X (the format's anonymous patient) when it is empty or anonymous. The start date and time are taken from info.

One 'EDF Annotations' signal carries the recording's annotations. Each data record opens with a time-keeping TAL of its own start time, which EDF+ requires, then one TAL per annotation that falls in the record's window: the onset, and the symbol as the text, or the aux text when the symbol is the note symbol.

The recording's length need not be a whole number of records; the last partial record is padded with the digital minimum, and info.padded says so, because those padded samples read back as the physical minimum of each lead.

The EDF+ file itself is written by the edf toolbox, a dependency of this module, so the header layout and the little-endian samples are produced in one place; this writer only maps the ecglab recording onto the neutral struct it consumes.

xmldoc.bibliography: Kemp and Olivan, European data format 'plus' (EDF+), Clinical Neurophysiology 114(9), 2003.
